section: Civil Disobedience Movement - Lahore Session and Purna Swaraj, Dandi March, spread and phases
subsections: Lahore Session (Dec 1929) - president, Purna Swaraj, Independence Day
Dandi March - dates, ashram, route, marchers, Viceroy

accepted.s:
With reference to the Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress held in December 1929, consider the following statements:
1. The Nehru Report had demanded Dominion Status.
2. The one-year ultimatum given to the British at the Calcutta Session of 1928 had expired.
3. The Lahore Session accepted the Nehru Report without modification.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Nehru Report demanded Dominion Status, and the one-year ultimatum issued at Calcutta in 1928 had expired. The Lahore Session rejected the demand for Dominion Status and adopted Purna Swaraj.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that reverses the decision taken at Lahore.
accepted.sec: Lahore Session (Dec 1929) - president, Purna Swaraj, Independence Day

accepted.s: The Nehru Report of 1928 was prepared by the committee of the All Parties Conference under the chairmanship of:
accepted.x: The committee that prepared the Nehru Report was chaired by Motilal Nehru. Jawaharlal Nehru served as its secretary.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the chairman from the secretary in a committee-based question.
accepted.sec: Lahore Session (Dec 1929) - president, Purna Swaraj, Independence Day

accepted.s: Who was the first to pass a Purna Swaraj resolution at the district level in Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: Bulusu Sambamurthy of East Godavari was associated with the first district-level Purna Swaraj resolution in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Use the place-name clue to identify the associated Andhra leader.
accepted.sec: Lahore Session (Dec 1929) - president, Purna Swaraj, Independence Day

accepted.s: Who hoisted the national flag at Machilipatnam on 26 January 1930?
accepted.x: Thota Narsaiah hoisted the flag at Machilipatnam on 26 January 1930, which was observed as the first Independence Day.
accepted.tq: Match the specific Andhra place with the associated person.
accepted.sec: Lahore Session (Dec 1929) - president, Purna Swaraj, Independence Day

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relationship between the Calcutta Session of 1928 and the Lahore Session of 1929?
o: Calcutta accepted Dominion Status with a one-year ultimatum, while Lahore adopted Purna Swaraj after the ultimatum expired.
Calcutta adopted Purna Swaraj, while Lahore accepted Dominion Status.
Both sessions adopted Dominion Status without any time limit.
Both sessions adopted Purna Swaraj as the immediate objective.
accepted.x: The Calcutta Session accepted the Nehru Report's demand for Dominion Status and gave the British one year. After the ultimatum lapsed, the Lahore Session adopted Purna Swaraj.
accepted.tq: Contrast the decisions of two successive Congress sessions.
accepted.sec: Lahore Session (Dec 1929) - president, Purna Swaraj, Independence Day

accepted.s: The Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress in December 1929 was held during the viceroyalty of:
accepted.x: Lord Irwin was the Viceroy of India during the Lahore Session of December 1929 and during the beginning of the Civil Disobedience Movement.
accepted.tq: Apply the ruler–event association trap.
accepted.sec: Lahore Session (Dec 1929) - president, Purna Swaraj, Independence Day

accepted.s: Gandhi's letter containing eleven demands was sent to Viceroy Irwin on:
accepted.x: Gandhi sent the letter containing eleven demands to Irwin on 2 March 1930. The Dandi March began after the demands were ignored.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the date of the ultimatum from the dates of the march.
accepted.sec: Dandi March - dates, ashram, route, marchers, Viceroy

accepted.s: Which of the following was central among Gandhi's demands addressed to Viceroy Irwin before the Dandi March?
o: Acceptance of the Nehru Report without change
Immediate convening of the Third Round Table Conference
accepted.x: Abolition of the salt tax was a central demand in Gandhi's eleven-point letter to Viceroy Irwin. Irwin did not accept the demands.
accepted.tq: Identify the policy demand directly connected with the chosen symbol of protest.
accepted.sec: Dandi March - dates, ashram, route, marchers, Viceroy

accepted.s: How many followers accompanied Gandhi at the beginning of the Dandi March?
accepted.x: Gandhi began the Dandi March from Sabarmati Ashram with 78 followers.
accepted.tq: Use the exact numerical detail rather than the rounded distance or duration.
accepted.sec: Dandi March - dates, ashram, route, marchers, Viceroy

accepted.s: The approximate distance covered by the Dandi March from Sabarmati to Dandi was:
accepted.x: The march covered approximately 240 miles, or about 385 kilometres, through Gujarat to the coast at Dandi.
accepted.tq: Test the paired imperial and metric figures together.
accepted.sec: Dandi March - dates, ashram, route, marchers, Viceroy

accepted.s: The Dandi March proceeded through which region before reaching its destination on the coast?
accepted.x: The march proceeded through Gujarat from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi on the Navsari coast.
accepted.tq: Use the route-location association rather than the starting-place association.
accepted.sec: Dandi March - dates, ashram, route, marchers, Viceroy

accepted.s: Who was the only Telugu marcher among Gandhi's followers in the Dandi March?
accepted.x: Yerneni, also written Erneni, Subrahmanyam of Krishna district was the only Telugu marcher among Gandhi's followers in the Dandi March.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Telugu participant in the march from Andhra leaders associated with other activities.
accepted.sec: Dandi March - dates, ashram, route, marchers, Viceroy

accepted.s: Yerneni Subrahmanyam, who participated in the Dandi March, later founded an ashram at:
accepted.x: Yerneni Subrahmanyam later founded an ashram at Komaravolu.
accepted.tq: Link the participant with the later institution associated with him.
accepted.sec: Dandi March - dates, ashram, route, marchers, Viceroy

accepted.s: Why did Gandhi choose salt as the central symbol of the Civil Disobedience Movement?
o: It was produced exclusively in Gujarat.
It was used only by the urban middle classes.
It was a universal necessity and the salt tax visibly represented colonial exploitation.
It was connected with the demand for separate electorates.
accepted.x: Salt was consumed by both rich and poor, and the salt tax and monopoly made it a visible symbol of colonial economic exploitation.
accepted.tq: Choose the option that combines the social reach and political significance of salt.
accepted.sec: Dandi March - dates, ashram, route, marchers, Viceroy

accepted.s: Gandhi named which person as the first successor to lead the movement after his arrest during the Salt Satyagraha?
accepted.x: Abbas Tyabji was designated as Gandhi's first successor after his arrest. Sarojini Naidu was named the second successor.
accepted.tq: Read the sequence carefully when two leaders are both associated with succession.
accepted.sec: Dandi March - dates, ashram, route, marchers, Viceroy

accepted.s: Who was designated as the second successor after Gandhi's arrest during the Salt Satyagraha?
accepted.x: Sarojini Naidu was designated as the second successor after Abbas Tyabji.
accepted.tq: Test the order of succession rather than merely identifying a participant.
accepted.sec: Dandi March - dates, ashram, route, marchers, Viceroy

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Simon Commission appointed
B. Lahore Session adopting Purna Swaraj
C. First Independence Day
D. Gandhi-Irwin Pact
accepted.x: The Simon Commission was appointed in November 1927, the Lahore Session was held in December 1929, 26 January 1930 was observed as the first Independence Day, and the Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on 5 March 1931.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two 1929–30 events.
accepted.sec: Chronology - Simon to later events

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Nehru Report
B. Dandi March
C. First Round Table Conference
D. Withdrawal of the Civil Disobedience Movement
accepted.x: The Nehru Report was prepared in 1928, the Dandi March took place from 12 March to 6 April 1930, the First Round Table Conference was held in November 1930, and the Civil Disobedience Movement was withdrawn in 1934.
accepted.tq: Use the fixed years 1928, 1930 and 1934 to order the events.
accepted.sec: Chronology - Simon to later events

accepted.s: Which one of the following chronological sequences is correct?
o: Gandhi-Irwin Pact → Communal Award → Poona Pact → withdrawal of CDM
Communal Award → Gandhi-Irwin Pact → Poona Pact → withdrawal of CDM
Gandhi-Irwin Pact → Poona Pact → Communal Award → withdrawal of CDM
Poona Pact → Communal Award → Gandhi-Irwin Pact → withdrawal of CDM
accepted.x: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed in 1931, the Communal Award and Poona Pact followed in 1932, and the Civil Disobedience Movement was withdrawn in 1934.
accepted.tq: Place events by year before distinguishing the two events of 1932.
accepted.sec: Chronology - Simon to later events

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Communal Award was announced in August 1932, while the Poona Pact was signed in September 1932. The other pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Find the near-date trap between two events of 1932.
accepted.sec: Chronology - Simon to later events

accepted.s:
Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the following events?
A. Chauri Chaura incident
B. Lahore Session and Purna Swaraj
C. Gandhi-Irwin Pact
D. Cripps Mission
accepted.x: The Chauri Chaura incident occurred in 1922, the Lahore Session in 1929, the Gandhi-Irwin Pact in 1931 and the Cripps Mission in 1942.
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence to the widely separated years 1922, 1929, 1931 and 1942.
accepted.sec: Chronology - Simon to later events

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Aruna Asaf Ali — first woman president of the INC in Kanpur
Sarojini Naidu — founded an ashram at Komaravolu
Duvvuri Subbamma — led the Dharasana raid
accepted.x: Kasturba Gandhi participated in protests and suffered imprisonment. Sarojini Naidu led the Dharasana raid, Aruna Asaf Ali was associated with the Quit India flag-hoisting, and Duvvuri Subbamma was an Andhra leader jailed during the CDM.
accepted.tq: Eliminate swapped person–role pairs.
accepted.sec: Women in CDM - role

accepted.s: Sarojini Naidu led the raid at:
accepted.x: Sarojini Naidu led the raid at the Dharasana Salt Works after Gandhi's arrest.
accepted.tq: Separate the Civil Disobedience role from the Quit India role of the same leader.
accepted.sec: Women in CDM - role

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding women's participation in the Civil Disobedience Movement is correct?
o: Women participated only after the withdrawal of the movement in 1934.
Women joined in massive numbers, including picketing liquor and foreign-cloth shops.
Women participated only in underground revolutionary activity.
Women were excluded from protests against colonial taxes.
accepted.x: The Civil Disobedience Movement marked the first occasion on which women participated in massive numbers. Their activities included picketing liquor shops and shops selling foreign cloth.
accepted.tq: Select the option that captures both the scale and forms of participation.
accepted.sec: Women in CDM - role

accepted.s: Who was the first woman arrested in Nellore in connection with the national movement?
accepted.x: Paturi Balasaraswatamma was the first woman arrested in Nellore in connection with the national movement.
accepted.tq: Match the specific Andhra district with its associated woman activist.
accepted.sec: Women in CDM - role

accepted.s: Which of the following women was associated with East Godavari in the Civil Disobedience Movement?
accepted.x: Palakojeti Shyamalamba was an Andhra woman associated with East Godavari. Sattaraju Mangamma was associated with Eluru.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Andhra place–person associations.
accepted.sec: Women in CDM - role

accepted.s: Sattaraju Mangamma was associated with which place?
accepted.x: Sattaraju Mangamma was associated with Eluru in the Civil Disobedience Movement.
accepted.tq: Use district-level association to discriminate among Andhra women activists.
accepted.sec: Women in CDM - role

accepted.s: Who gave all her jewellery to support the national movement?
accepted.x: Maganti Annapurna gave all her jewellery to support the national movement.
accepted.tq: Identify the distinctive personal contribution rather than a political office.
accepted.sec: Women in CDM - role

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about Duvvuri Subbamma is correct?
o: She hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank in 1942.
She led the Dharasana raid after Gandhi's arrest.
She was an Andhra woman leader from East Godavari who was jailed during the CDM.
She was the first Indian woman president of the INC.
accepted.x: Duvvuri Subbamma was an Andhra woman leader from East Godavari who was jailed during the Civil Disobedience Movement.
accepted.tq: Reject roles belonging to other prominent women leaders.
accepted.sec: Women in CDM - role

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about the Civil Disobedience Movement is/are correct?
1. It was the first movement in which women participated in massive numbers.
2. Picketing liquor shops was one form of women's participation.
3. Picketing shops selling foreign cloth was one form of women's participation.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Women participated on a large scale and undertook picketing of liquor and foreign-cloth shops.
accepted.tq: When all statements describe connected aspects of one participation pattern, test the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Women in CDM - role
